ryan: FYI saw a sharp drop in prefix/prompt cache hit rate after last night's attn-lowering + quant-profile rollout. web-gen latency also spiked a little. telemetry shows prefix_hit_rate from ~0.62 -> ~0.44 on the affected pool.

kate: ugh. did anything touch key derivation or tokenizer normalizations in that deploy?

ryan: not intentionally. deploy-note: kernel=attn-lower-v2, quant_profile=fastfp16-v2, compiler=matmul-rewrite-3. no explicit keying change in the runtime patch. but we did flip a heuristic in the attention path that touches padding handling.

jia: can you paste examples of keys that missed? comparing pre/post would help.

ryan: here's a pair from a repeated prompt; pre-upgrade hit key vs post-upgrade produced key (same prompt).
```
pre: prefix_key=CTX|toknorm=1|seed=0x9f4b|len=48|algo=v1
post: prefix_key=CTX|toknorm=1|seed=0x9f4b|len=48|algo=v1|pad_sig=1
```
looks like some additional pad_sig flag is getting appended for batched cases after the new kernel path.

mike: that aligns with the padding-handling tweak. We added a per-batch pad checksum to avoid stale KV reads when using packed kernels, but it should be optional. If pad_sig gets into the canonical key we won't match older cached entries.

kate: is pad_sig derived from batch shape or from tokenized content?

mike: from batch shape + trailing pad count. For single-request flows pad_sig is 0. For some of our web-gen traffic where we pack two short requests it became 1. Previously the runtime used a normalize step that dropped pad_sig from keys. The new path forgot that normalizer.

ryan: quick experiment: toggled kernel flag to force key normalization off the new path and warmed a small canary pool. hit rate recovered to ~0.61 within ~15 minutes. can we make that change hotfix?

jia: +1 for hotfix. We should also add a regression test that asserts key canonicalization invariants across kernel variants.

ops-bot: deploy started: rollback-quickfix/pad-key-normalization to pool web-gen-canary by ryan (sha: cb7a2)

kate: good. after canary looks stable, push to main. Also add a small profiler snapshot next deploy: run perf-profile --kv-keys --sample 1m on both kernels so we can diff key mutation rates.

mike: will add tests and a patch to ensure pad_sig is metadata-only (not part of the persisted key) unless a config flag is explicitly set. Also will add a metric pad_sig_in_keys_count.

ryan: notes for postmortem: root cause := kernel rework changed padding handling and accidentally included pad_sig in persisted prefix key. Impact := ~18-20% reduction in prefix hit rate for mixed-pack workloads, small latency increase and higher token cost. Remediation := rollback-ish hotfix + tests + telemetry.

jia: thanks. putting a quick runbook: if hit-rate drop >10% after future kernel flips, grep for key diffs: `kubectl logs runtime --since=10m | jq -r .kv_key | sort | uniq -c | head -n 20` and compare to previous build artifacts.

mike: I'll follow up with a PR that removes pad_sig from key serialization and adds a unit test.

ryan: closing loop: canary rolled to main at 3246803000, overall prefix hit normalized to previous baseline in ~25m. reopening follow-ups: add unit/regression tests + add pad_sig metric + include key-canonicalization check in canary gating.

kate: :thumbsup:, thanks everyone.
